title: Business Systems Engineer III, Metronome - Confluent
description: Introduction At IBM Finance & Operations, we are the backbone of IBM’s transformation driving efficiency, transparency, and smart decision-making across the business. Our teams provide the insight and discipline that guide strategy, ensure financial strength, and enable IBM to invest in innovation and growth. Working in Finance & Operations means combining analytical skills with collaboration and curiosity. You’ll partner with colleagues across functions and geographies, using data, technology, and process excellence to create solutions that improve performance and deliver measurable impact. IBM offers continuous learning, career development, and a culture that values diverse perspectives. Join us and be part of a global team that keeps IBM moving forward, while building your own future in a dynamic and evolving environment. Your Role and Responsibilities About the Role Confluent’s Business Systems team is looking for a Business Systems Engineer III to help build and operate the systems that power a modern, consumption-based SaaS business. In this role, you will be a hands-on technical owner for executing improvements and enhancements in the Metronome platform. You will configure, design, develop, test, deploy, and debug business systems solutions that support usage, pricing, billing, entitlements, invoicing, and related financial processes. You will work closely with experienced engineers, business systems partners, Finance, Revenue Operations, Engineering, Data, and other stakeholders to turn well-defined business needs into reliable production outcomes. This is an execution-focused role for an engineer who takes pride in quality, learns complex systems quickly, and delivers with speed. You will work within established architecture and delivery patterns while building the judgment to identify risks, clarify requirements, and recommend better approaches. Your work will directly improve the reliability, scalability, and usability of systems that are critical to Confluent’s business. What You Will Do Own the delivery of moderate-complexity Metronome enhancements from technical discovery and implementation through testing, deployment, and post-release validation. Configure and extend Metronome to support usage, pricing, rating, billing, entitlement, invoicing, and downstream financial workflows. Translate business requirements and solution designs into clear technical tasks, configurations, code changes, test cases, and release plans. Develop platform customizations, scripts, APIs, integrations, and automation using established patterns and sound engineering practices. Design and implement changes that are readable, testable, secure, maintainable, and resilient to expected edge cases and errors. Build and execute unit, integration, regression, and user acceptance testing for system changes; investigate failures and drive issues to resolution. Deploy changes using established version-control, release-management, change-management, and production-readiness practices. Debug issues across configurations, code, integrations, data, and dependent systems; use a systematic approach to isolate root causes and implement durable fixes. Trace data flows and dependencies across Metronome and connected systems, identifying downstream impacts before changes are released. Maintain clear technical documentation, deployment notes, test evidence, troubleshooting guidance, and operational runbooks. Participate in design reviews, code reviews, backlog refinement, planning, and other delivery ceremonies; provide constructive input and ask effective questions. Communicate progress, risks, blockers, and tradeoffs clearly, escalating decisions that require broader architectural or business judgment. Partner with business stakeholders and technical teams to clarify requirements, validate outcomes, and deliver solutions that improve operational efficiency. Contribute to shared engineering practices, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement across the Business Systems team. Required Skills 5+ years of experience in business systems engineering, software engineering, systems development, application administration, or a related field; equivalent practical experience is welcome. Hands-on experience configuring, developing, testing, deploying, and supporting complex SaaS business-system solutions. Experience with Metronome or another usage-based billing, consumption management, metering, subscription billing, or revenue operations platform is strongly preferred. Working knowledge of API-first integration patterns, Python REST APIs, webhooks, JSON, data models, SQL, scripting, and asynchronous system behavior. Ability to navigate a complex system, understand how components fit together, and trace a change across configurations, integrations, data, and dependent services. Strong engineering discipline, including writing maintainable code or configuration, accounting for edge cases, handling errors, protecting sensitive data, and creating effective tests. Experience with modern software delivery practices such as Git-based development, code review, automated testing, CI/CD, release management, and production support. A systematic approach to debugging and problem solving, with the ability to resolve issues within your area of ownership and recognize when escalation is needed. Ability to manage your own work, break larger tasks into workable milestones, meet commitments, and move quickly without sacrificing quality. Strong attention to detail and follow-through, especially when changes affect financially significant data or business processes. Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical work to business stakeholders and collaborate effectively with engineers and partners. A customer-focused, collaborative mindset and a desire to simplify processes, remove manual work, and improve the experience of the teams who rely on Business Systems. Preferred Skills Experience implementing or operating Metronome in a high-growth SaaS environment. Experience integrating usage and billing platforms with Salesforce, CPQ, NetSuite or another ERP, contract lifecycle management systems, data warehouses, or internal services. Familiarity with consumption-based pricing, product catalogs, usage data quality, entitlements, invoicing, credits, collections, or revenue operations. Experience supporting high-volume usage data, event-driven integrations, or financially significant business processes. Familiarity with cloud platforms, infrastructure-as-code, observability tooling, and secure service-to-service integrations. Experience working in an environment with access controls, audit trails, change management, data governance, or SOX-related controls. Experience improving deployment automation, test coverage, documentation, monitoring, or developer productivity. Thoughtful use of AI-assisted development and automation, paired with sound judgment, human review, testing, and appropriate controls. Additional Details When applying to jobs of your interest, we recommend that you do so for those that match your experience and expertise. Our recruiters advise that you apply to not more than 3 roles in a year for the best candidate experience. For additional information about location requirements, please discuss with the recruiter following submission of your application.

From day one, IBMers have the trust to create incredible things that alter the future for us, for each other, for our clients — and for the world.

Around the globe, we’re constantly evolving who we are, adapting with purpose, and building an environment where everyone thrives, both individually and collectively. title: Software Engineer
description: Itron is innovating new ways for utilities and cities to manage energy and water. We create a more resourceful world to protect essential resources for today and tomorrow. Join us. Itron Resiliency Solutions is an innovative business unit within Itron focused on solving mission critical problems for utilities through software and AI. Resiliency Solutions offers unique, market leading solutions for front-line worker safety, storm response, excavation damage prevention, construction management, and many more. These software and AI solutions solve end-to-end challenges for the utilities that power our society and are used by the largest and most complex organizations in the world such as National Grid, Southern Company, and Exelon. Itron Resiliency Solutions is a global, diverse team of builders and innovators who tackle previously impossible challenges for our customers. If you have a desire to challenge yourself, solve impactful problems, and work with a passionate and talented team, this is the place. The Emergency Preparedness & Response (EP&R) team builds the systems that keep critical operations running when it matters most. When storms and severe weather threaten communities and infrastructure across the US, our platform enables customers to rapidly procure, mobilize, and manage the workforce needed to respond to and recover from storm damage — often under tight timelines and high-stakes conditions. We are looking for a Principal Engineer who is deeply hands-on, works backward from customer pain points and business needs, and measures success by impact rather than lines of code shipped. You will be the technical anchor of the team: a backend-heavy full-stack engineer who knows our systems inside and out, reasons rigorously about trade-offs, and raises the engineering bar for everyone around you while leading the team toward outcomes that genuinely matter. About the role We're hiring a Software Engineer in Bengaluru to build and run production services. You'll own features end to end — from understanding the problem to shipping, monitoring and fixing what you built — with growing independence and support from senior engineers. Our India engineering team is taking full ownership of core products and growing quickly, including a ground-up rebuild of a customer-critical service. You'll work closely with senior engineers, your Engineering Manager, Product and Customer Support. What you'll own in your first year Own: Own features and services end to end with speed and quality — build, test, release, monitor, fix. Well-scoped problems, then bigger ones. Start with clearly defined work and grow into breaking down ambiguous problems yourself. Design. Write design notes for your features and get them reviewed; contribute to larger designs led by senior engineers. Quality. Write tests, add observability, and take part in on-call so issues are caught before customers see them. Customers. Understand who uses what you build, and learn from support issues what to fix next. Code reviews. Give and receive thoughtful reviews, and help onboard engineers who join after you. What you must bring These are the bar. We can't teach them on the job. Experience: 1–4 years building production software. We level on demonstrated scope, not years alone. You've shipped code that runs in production. Features or services you built, released and supported — not only coursework or prototypes. You are strong at problem solving. You can take an unfamiliar, feature-sized problem, reason through it, and land on a simple, correct solution. You work independently toward a clear goal. Given a clear goal, you figure out the steps, unblock yourself, and ask for help at the right moments. We care how you engineer more than which language you did it in. Technical background You've built production software with a modern stack, such as: Cloud: hands-on with AWS — you've deployed and debugged services running on it. Languages: strong in at least one modern language such as Python, Java or JavaScript/TypeScript. Frameworks: modern service frameworks such as FastAPI, Node.js or equivalents. Databases: solid data modeling and query fundamentals — you can design a schema, use indexes well, and explain why a query is slow and how you'd fix it. Fundamentals: data structures, API design, and the basics of caching and concurrency. Exact tools matter less than depth. Strong experience on an equivalent stack is welcome. What sets great candidates apart Impact you can explain. You can say what changed because of something you built — for users, performance or reliability. One problem you went deep on. A bug, a performance issue or a design where you dug past the surface to understand why. Ownership beyond the ticket. You've fixed what you shipped when it broke, and improved it after release without being asked. Framework mindset: You notice repeated code and turn it into something reusable. Learning speed. You've picked up a new domain, codebase or technology quickly and delivered in it. Curiosity about the user. You've asked why a requirement exists, or suggested a simpler way to solve the user's problem. What we look for in everyone we hire Whatever the role, we hire for six things. Customer obsession. You care who uses what you build and whether it actually helped them. Impact over activity. You measure success by outcomes, not tickets closed or lines written. Honesty. You're specific about your own part in team work, raise problems early, and say what didn't work. Independence. You don't wait to be told every next step. You figure things out with little hand-holding. You will work with leaders who will partner with you in the journey. Passion. Not the word on a resume — the evidence: a side project, a technology you went deep on, something you built because you wanted to. Depth. At least one thing you've built or debugged that you can explain down to the internals and the tradeoffs. Itron is committed to building an inclusive and diverse workforce and providing an authentic workplace experience for all employees. If you are excited about this role but your past experiences don't perfectly align with every requirement, we encourage you to apply anyway. In the end, you may be just who we are looking for! The successful candidate's starting wage will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills and experience. Itron is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. If you require an accommodation to apply, please contact a recruiting representative at 1-800-635-5461 or email Accessibility@itron.com. Itron is transforming how the world manages energy, water and city services. Our trusted intelligent infrastructure solutions help utilities and cities improve efficiency, build resilience and deliver safe, reliable and affordable service. With edge intelligence, we connect people, data insights and devices so communities can better manage the essential resources they rely on to live. Join us as we create a more resourceful world: www.itron.com

Dexcom Corporation (NASDAQ DXCM) is a pioneer and global leader in continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). Since 1999, Dexcom has developed innovative technology that has transformed how people manage diabetes. Dexcom has done this through sensor and software innovation to meet the unique needs of people with diabetes, their caregivers, and health care professionals. Dexcom has also led innovative advocacy work to ensure CGM technology can be accessible for more people around the world.

title: Junior Data Scientists
description: Job Requirements Role: To contribute to the end-to-end development and product lifecycle management of artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) systems as part of an R&D organization. The Junior Data Scientist supports the definition of intended algorithm performance, the development and curation of representative data and annotations, the development of AI/ML algorithms, and the generation of scientific evidence demonstrating stand-alone algorithm performance. The candidate is expected to: Apply scientific, statistical, machine learning, and software engineering methods to develop and evaluate AI/ML algorithm components for defined product use cases. Work with experienced Data Scientists, product management, clinical or domain experts, software developers, and quality and regulatory functions to translate customer needs and the intended use into measurable algorithm performance targets. Support the definition, sourcing, curation, documentation, and maintenance of representative data cohorts and annotations required for training, tuning, and evaluation. Plan and execute reproducible scientific evaluations that provide objective evidence of algorithm performance, limitations, and suitability for the intended use. Contribute the Data Science work products and evidence required for integration of AI/ML algorithm components into products and for their verification, validation, regulatory release, and lifecycle monitoring. What are my responsibilities? As a Junior Data Scientist, you are required to: Support the finalization of product and algorithm concepts by translating customer needs, intended use, clinical or technical requirements, and applicable regulatory considerations into measurable state-of-the-art performance targets. Contribute to the definition of the AI/ML development and scientific evaluation strategy for assigned algorithm components under the guidance of experienced Data Scientists. Perform exploratory data analysis and data risk assessments to identify data gaps, quality issues, potential bias, confounding factors, outliers, and limitations that may affect algorithm development or evaluation. Define and document data needs for training, tuning, and evaluation, including relevant subgroups and acceptance criteria, so that data cohorts are representative of the intended use and aligned with the product and regulatory strategy. Support the specification of annotations, acceptance criteria, and quality controls; collaborate with qualified internal or external suppliers on sourcing data and annotations. Curate, version, maintain, and document representative data cohorts and ensure data provenance, traceability, quality, and fitness for purpose together with data management stakeholders. Design, implement, train, tune, and technically characterize AI/ML algorithm components using appropriate machine learning, deep learning, statistical, or generative AI methods. Define scientifically justified metrics, evaluation methods, test cases, and acceptance criteria to assess stand-alone algorithm performance, including relevant aspects such as accuracy, robustness, reliability, generalizability, explainability, bias, and subgroup performance. Implement and execute reproducible bench tests on representative evaluation cohorts and relevant subgroups as part of the verification and validation strategy. Analyze and interpret evaluation results, investigate failure modes, document residual limitations, and derive evidence-based recommendations for algorithm improvement and product decisions. Document development and evaluation activities and contribute to Data Science work products such as data management information, annotation specifications, scientific evaluation test cases, and scientific evaluation reports. Provide scientific evidence and technical input for product reviews and regulatory submissions and support responses to questions concerning data, annotations, evaluation methods, and stand-alone algorithm performance. Support the design and execution of clinical investigations, reader studies, or other studies when additional evidence is required by the product or regulatory strategy. Collaborate with software engineering and MLOps functions to establish reproducible pipelines, versioned artifacts, automated tests, controlled deployment, and integration of algorithm components into the product. Help define and implement monitoring metrics for detecting data anomalies, outliers, and algorithm performance drift across the product lifecycle. Regularly review advances in Data Science and AI and assess their applicability to the development and evaluation of AI/ML products. Qualification: Master's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Biomedical Engineering, Medical Informatics, or a related quantitative or engineering field. A Ph.D. is welcome but not required. The candidate should have completed university-level coursework or equivalent practical training in: Probability, statistics, and experimental design Artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep learning Linear algebra, optimization, and numerical methods Data structures, algorithms, and software programming Model evaluation, scientific methodology, and interpretation of empirical results Experience level: This is a junior R&D position. Relevant experience may have been gained through academic research, a thesis, internships, working-student assignments, or up to approximately three years of professional work in Data Science, machine learning, AI research, or AI/ML product development. Demonstrated hands-on experience in developing and scientifically evaluating AI/ML models is more important than a specific number of years. Desired Knowledge & Experience: Sound understanding of machine learning, deep learning, statistical analysis, experimental design, and model evaluation. Active programming skills in Python and practical experience with libraries and frameworks such as NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow, or Keras. Hands-on experience with the development workflow of AI/ML models, including data preparation, training, tuning, evaluation, error analysis, reproducibility, and documentation. Ability to define meaningful performance metrics, evaluation cohorts, subgroup analyses, test methods, and acceptance criteria for the intended use of an AI/ML algorithm. Understanding of data quality, representativeness, bias, annotation quality, data provenance, and traceability in AI/ML development. Knowledge of Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) concepts and tooling, including source and data versioning, reproducible pipelines, experiment tracking, automated testing, CI/CD, deployment, and monitoring. Hands-on exposure to current Large Language Models and Generative AI, including foundation models, prompting, retrieval-augmented generation, and model adaptation or fine-tuning. Knowledge of Agentic AI, including tool-using models, multi-step workflows, orchestration, memory, and autonomous or semi-autonomous decision paths, is an advantage. Experience or strong interest in the systematic evaluation of LLM, Generative AI, and Agentic AI systems, including task-specific benchmarks, groundedness and factuality, robustness, reproducibility, human evaluation, safety and guardrail testing, tool-use correctness, and analysis of failure modes. Experience with databases and query languages such as SQL; knowledge of Kusto Query Language, Snowflake, or graph databases such as Neo4j is an advantage. Exposure to cloud-based data and AI environments, preferably Microsoft Azure, such as Azure Blob Storage, Azure Databricks, Azure Data Factory, Azure Machine Learning, Azure Monitor, or Azure DevOps. Experience with structured and unstructured data, for example machine logs, event data, Parquet files, text data, or multimodal data. Knowledge of healthcare, medical technology, clinical data, or interoperability standards such as DICOM is preferred. Basic project management skills and familiarity with working in cross-functional R&D or product-development teams. Required Soft Skills & Other Capabilities: Scientific mindset, strong analytical ability, and attention to detail. Commitment to objective evidence, reproducibility, traceability, data integrity, and responsible AI development. Curiosity and resilience to investigate unexpected results, challenge assumptions, and improve models based on evidence. Collaborative approach to working with Data Scientists, domain experts, software engineers, product management, and quality and regulatory stakeholders. Ability to work independently within an agreed scope and to seek guidance when technical, scientific, product, or regulatory implications require alignment. Clear written and verbal communication skills in English, including the ability to explain methods, results, uncertainties, limitations, and risks to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

description: Job Requirements Role: To contribute to the end-to-end development and product lifecycle management of artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) systems as part of an R&D organization. The Junior Data Scientist supports the definition of intended algorithm performance, the development and curation of representative data and annotations, the development of AI/ML algorithms, and the generation of scientific evidence demonstrating stand-alone algorithm performance. The candidate is expected to: Apply scientific, statistical, machine learning, and software engineering methods to develop and evaluate AI/ML algorithm components for defined product use cases. Work with experienced Data Scientists, product management, clinical or domain experts, software developers, and quality and regulatory functions to translate customer needs and the intended use into measurable algorithm performance targets. Support the definition, sourcing, curation, documentation, and maintenance of representative data cohorts and annotations required for training, tuning, and evaluation. Plan and execute reproducible scientific evaluations that provide objective evidence of algorithm performance, limitations, and suitability for the intended use. Contribute the Data Science work products and evidence required for integration of AI/ML algorithm components into products and for their verification, validation, regulatory release, and lifecycle monitoring. What are my responsibilities? As a Junior Data Scientist, you are required to: Support the finalization of product and algorithm concepts by translating customer needs, intended use, clinical or technical requirements, and applicable regulatory considerations into measurable state-of-the-art performance targets. Contribute to the definition of the AI/ML development and scientific evaluation strategy for assigned algorithm components under the guidance of experienced Data Scientists. Perform exploratory data analysis and data risk assessments to identify data gaps, quality issues, potential bias, confounding factors, outliers, and limitations that may affect algorithm development or evaluation. Define and document data needs for training, tuning, and evaluation, including relevant subgroups and acceptance criteria, so that data cohorts are representative of the intended use and aligned with the product and regulatory strategy. Support the specification of annotations, acceptance criteria, and quality controls; collaborate with qualified internal or external suppliers on sourcing data and annotations. Curate, version, maintain, and document representative data cohorts and ensure data provenance, traceability, quality, and fitness for purpose together with data management stakeholders. Design, implement, train, tune, and technically characterize AI/ML algorithm components using appropriate machine learning, deep learning, statistical, or generative AI methods. Define scientifically justified metrics, evaluation methods, test cases, and acceptance criteria to assess stand-alone algorithm performance, including relevant aspects such as accuracy, robustness, reliability, generalizability, explainability, bias, and subgroup performance. Implement and execute reproducible bench tests on representative evaluation cohorts and relevant subgroups as part of the verification and validation strategy. Analyze and interpret evaluation results, investigate failure modes, document residual limitations, and derive evidence-based recommendations for algorithm improvement and product decisions. Document development and evaluation activities and contribute to Data Science work products such as data management information, annotation specifications, scientific evaluation test cases, and scientific evaluation reports. Provide scientific evidence and technical input for product reviews and regulatory submissions and support responses to questions concerning data, annotations, evaluation methods, and stand-alone algorithm performance. Support the design and execution of clinical investigations, reader studies, or other studies when additional evidence is required by the product or regulatory strategy. Collaborate with software engineering and MLOps functions to establish reproducible pipelines, versioned artifacts, automated tests, controlled deployment, and integration of algorithm components into the product. Help define and implement monitoring metrics for detecting data anomalies, outliers, and algorithm performance drift across the product lifecycle. Regularly review advances in Data Science and AI and assess their applicability to the development and evaluation of AI/ML products. Qualification: Master's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Biomedical Engineering, Medical Informatics, or a related quantitative or engineering field. A Ph.D. is welcome but not required. The candidate should have completed university-level coursework or equivalent practical training in: Probability, statistics, and experimental design Artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep learning Linear algebra, optimization, and numerical methods Data structures, algorithms, and software programming Model evaluation, scientific methodology, and interpretation of empirical results Experience level: This is a junior R&D position. Relevant experience may have been gained through academic research, a thesis, internships, working-student assignments, or up to approximately three years of professional work in Data Science, machine learning, AI research, or AI/ML product development. Demonstrated hands-on experience in developing and scientifically evaluating AI/ML models is more important than a specific number of years. Desired Knowledge & Experience: Sound understanding of machine learning, deep learning, statistical analysis, experimental design, and model evaluation. Active programming skills in Python and practical experience with libraries and frameworks such as NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow, or Keras. Hands-on experience with the development workflow of AI/ML models, including data preparation, training, tuning, evaluation, error analysis, reproducibility, and documentation. Ability to define meaningful performance metrics, evaluation cohorts, subgroup analyses, test methods, and acceptance criteria for the intended use of an AI/ML algorithm. Understanding of data quality, representativeness, bias, annotation quality, data provenance, and traceability in AI/ML development. Knowledge of Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) concepts and tooling, including source and data versioning, reproducible pipelines, experiment tracking, automated testing, CI/CD, deployment, and monitoring. Hands-on exposure to current Large Language Models and Generative AI, including foundation models, prompting, retrieval-augmented generation, and model adaptation or fine-tuning. Knowledge of Agentic AI, including tool-using models, multi-step workflows, orchestration, memory, and autonomous or semi-autonomous decision paths, is an advantage. Experience or strong interest in the systematic evaluation of LLM, Generative AI, and Agentic AI systems, including task-specific benchmarks, groundedness and factuality, robustness, reproducibility, human evaluation, safety and guardrail testing, tool-use correctness, and analysis of failure modes. Experience with databases and query languages such as SQL; knowledge of Kusto Query Language, Snowflake, or graph databases such as Neo4j is an advantage. Exposure to cloud-based data and AI environments, preferably Microsoft Azure, such as Azure Blob Storage, Azure Databricks, Azure Data Factory, Azure Machine Learning, Azure Monitor, or Azure DevOps. Experience with structured and unstructured data, for example machine logs, event data, Parquet files, text data, or multimodal data. Knowledge of healthcare, medical technology, clinical data, or interoperability standards such as DICOM is preferred. Basic project management skills and familiarity with working in cross-functional R&D or product-development teams. Required Soft Skills & Other Capabilities: Scientific mindset, strong analytical ability, and attention to detail. Commitment to objective evidence, reproducibility, traceability, data integrity, and responsible AI development. Curiosity and resilience to investigate unexpected results, challenge assumptions, and improve models based on evidence. Collaborative approach to working with Data Scientists, domain experts, software engineers, product management, and quality and regulatory stakeholders. Ability to work independently within an agreed scope and to seek guidance when technical, scientific, product, or regulatory implications require alignment. Clear written and verbal communication skills in English, including the ability to explain methods, results, uncertainties, limitations, and risks to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
